case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread discusses Bluetooth qualification planning for a product based on a previously qualified controller design. The customer asks what evidence is required for qualification, what testing must be performed, how long registration takes after test data submission, and whether qualification can be handled outside Japan. The consultant clarifies that the product requires RF/RF PHY testing on the end-product hardware and that qualification can be managed through BQTFs in different countries. The discussion also explains how to determine required test coverage from ICS selections and Bluetooth test specifications.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The referenced controller design is an SoC, so Bluetooth qualification requires RF/RF PHY testing on the customer's product board rather than relying solely on the controller listing. Required test coverage must match the RF and RF PHY features enabled in the ICS, including the supported RF class and PHY capabilities listed in the referenced design. A BQTF-issued RF/RF PHY test report covering all applicable ICS-supported functions is required when the customer provides its own measurement data. The thread explains that test cases can be derived from the RF and RF PHY Test Specifications by using the Test Case Mapping sections and matching them to ICS items marked as supported. The consultant also confirms that profile testing is not required because the referenced design already covers those profile layers.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The qualification requirements are driven by the referenced design structure and the product's ICS-supported functionality. Because the referenced item is a controller-level design, the end product must demonstrate compliance through RF/RF PHY testing of the finished product hardware. Test obligations are determined by the RF and RF PHY features declared in the ICS, and the submitted BQTF test report must cover all corresponding required test cases. Profile-layer testing can be omitted when those functions are already covered by the referenced qualified design.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If the customer submits incomplete RF/RF PHY evidence that does not cover all ICS-supported functions, the qualification package may be incomplete and require rework. Misunderstanding which tests are required could result in missing mandatory test coverage, delays to registration, and product launch schedule impact. Assuming that a controller reference alone eliminates all testing obligations could lead to insufficient qualification evidence being collected.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When qualifying a product that references an existing controller or SoC design, do not assume all testing can be reused. First determine the referenced design type, then map the product's ICS-supported RF and RF PHY features to the applicable Test Case Mapping tables to identify the exact test evidence required. Reuse of profile qualification does not automatically eliminate RF/RF PHY obligations on the finished product.
